headline: Executive order starts the process of labeling Ansar Allah, the Yemen-based group known as the Houthis, a Foreign Terrorist Organization.
what_it_does: This order deals with naming Ansar Allah, also called the Houthis, as a Foreign Terrorist Organization under U.S. law. No summary was provided, so the exact steps, deadlines, and agency duties in the order are not described here. In general, this kind of label makes it a crime to knowingly give the group money or other support. It can also lead to its funds being frozen and its members being kept out of the United States.

who_it_affects.group: Members and supporters of Ansar Allah (the Houthis)
who_it_affects.how: A terrorist label generally bars them from entering the U.S. and allows their money held by U.S. banks to be frozen.

who_it_affects.group: People and organizations that deal with the Houthis or work in areas they control, including aid groups in Yemen
who_it_affects.how: They could face legal risk if they knowingly provide money, goods, or services that count as support to the group.

who_it_affects.group: Banks and other U.S. financial institutions
who_it_affects.how: They may have to block and report any funds linked to the group.

when_it_takes_effect: The order was signed January 22, 2025. The source does not say when a final designation takes effect.
